rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-phase failure mode + escape hatch.
rules_evaluated.evidence: HARM §47 prevents: a trainer meeting a real in-room failure with no recovery move. Present here in §47's own INVERTED form — the clause 'Source keeps the departed beat's apparatus … promises outcomes it no longer produces' fires exactly. L163 rows a phase that does not exist: '| Phase 3 — *"settle the `observations/` tree on disk before the send-off"* | student plans the tidy-up in chat but never lands the diff | Trainer: *"show me the diff landed before you paste the send-off."* |'. Verified mechanically: `grep -n '^## ' curriculum/exercises/walk-and-send-off.md` → 'Phase 1: Pick the task…' and 'Phase 2: Build the ranked list…' only; same command on set-the-markers-send-it-off.md → 'Phase 1: Set the two return markers' and 'Phase 2: Send it off'. There is no Phase 3 in M4. `grep -rn 'Phase 3'` across both exercises + this module + trainer-modules.md returns Phase 3 ONLY inside this file's maintainer block (L133, L134, L163); the trainer-modules.md hits at L391/L401 are M5's verifier phase. Worse than a stale label: the beat itself was deliberately retired to optional prose — walk-and-send-off L163 states '`walk-and-send-off-4` stays retired. The settle-the-tree beat runs as plain body prose … Do not re-fence it', and the student-facing line at walk-and-send-off L79 reads 'Optional, before the send-off: tidy the folder.' So L163 and L134 ('Confirm the tidy-up diff landed before the send-off') hand the trainer a mandatory demand for a diff on a beat the body marks Optional — a live contradiction delivered in the room, against a phase number that does not exist.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Retire the Phase 3 row and the two Phase 3 decision-point lines, or re-attach the settle failure/escape to the beat's real home (close of walk-and-send-off Phase 2) in the register the body actually uses — optional, not 'show me the diff'.

Carry the open question into Module 5'; (3) the receiving lecture declares the handoff deliberate in its own backing block ('the M4→M5 gap read that hands the student the term before this slide'), so the earlier placement is recorded at both ends per §9b; (4) the closer is self-sufficient — it names and defines Sutton in-body and cannot depend on an optional read. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Judge-owned: prep-load ceiling on the five-entry Module 5 pre-read block.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Load re-derived from primary sources, not from the brief: Mollick 10 (L109) + clean-code-is-steering 1404 body words ≈ 7 + Entis/Klaassen video 30 + verification-asymmetry 353 body words ≈ 2 + Klaassen guide 15-20 = ~64-69 min across five entries, of which 30 min is one optional video and ~9 min is two internal supplementaries. Corpus precedent verified and it holds: getting-going.md L119 prices the M1→M2 gap at 5+30+10+15 = 60 min across four entries, so this is the second instance of an established shape, not an outlier — the L94 accept-note's appeal to that precedent is accurate. What the precedent does NOT cover is the asymmetry: `grep -n '^## ' getting-going.md` shows no Bring section, so the M1→M2 gap is reading-only, whereas this gap ALSO carries a doing obligation (L62-64, a session that produced something plus a scrollback read). The honest verdict on the ceiling: ~65 minutes across five items is past what a working engineer does in one evening on top of a run, and the block is right not to pretend otherwise. 'Start with the first' (L70) is a REAL mitigation, not a fig leaf — it creates and names a 10-minute compliant path, and the design intent at L94 (Mollick first so a student meeting the other four cold does not build gates for their own sake) survives the most likely outcome of read-one-skim-none. It is a HALF mitigation, because the block never states a floor: 'The rest point at the same surprise' (L74) presents the remaining four as a set, so the student who stops after Mollick has no signal that they are done rather than behind. The stronger, checkable defect is that the frame which makes ~65 min make sense is filed on the wrong side of the gap. `learn-from-the-test.md` L9 reads 'Optional prep while it's still running' — the reading is designed for the dead time inside the un-watched send-off, which is exactly the right use of a walk-away wait (§1). The student meets that framing only AFTER the gap has passed. Both halves of the fix are one sentence in this file's L70 lede.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: In L70, carry M5's own frame back across the gap and state the floor: name that these are for the wait while the session runs, and that the first one alone is a complete answer.
